la:adj:innumerabilis.html:
in-nŭmĕrābĭlis, e, adj.,
countless, innumerable (class.): mundi,; : atomi,: homines,: pecunia,: series annorum,: numerus annorum,.— Absol.: reperiam multos vel innumerabiles potius quibus, etc.,; ; cf. innumerabilia,; .—Adv.: innŭmĕrābĭlĭter, innumerably, ; ;

la:adj:innuptus.gloss: unmarried (said of women), single, without a husband
senses: unmarried (said of women), single, without a husband
la:adj:innuptus.html:
in-nuptus, a, um, adj.
2. in-nubo
,
unmarried.
Lit.
Adj.: pueri innuptaeque puellae,: Minerva,virginal, virgin-,: manus,the Amazons,.—
Subst.: innupta, ae, f., an unmarried woman, a virgin, ; ; ; 64, 78; ; : praegnans,.—
Transf.: innuptae nuptiae (γάμος ἄγαμος), a marriage that is no marriage, an unhappy marriage, Poëta ap. (Trag. Fragm. Inc. v. 80 Rib.).

la:adj:innoxius.html:
in-noxĭus, a, um, adj.,
harmless, innoxious.
Act.
In gen.: quaedam animalia indigenis innoxia,: vitis viribus (bibentium),: anguis,: vulnera,not mortal, curable,: saltus,free from noxious animals,: iter,secure,: hinc vel illinc appellere indiscretum et innoxium est,fin.—
That does harm to none, not guilty, blameless, innocent: decet innocentem servum atque innoxium,; : non possum innoxia dici,: animus innoxior (al. innoxiior), Cato ap. P.: paupertas,undeserved poverty,.—
With gen.: criminis innoxia,: initi consilii in caput regis,.—
With a and abl.: ut innoxium abs te atque abs tuis me inrideas,i. e. who never harmed you or yours,.—
Pass., unharmed, unhurt, uninjured: innoxius volvitur in flammis,: hi magistratus, provincias aliaque omnia tenere, ipsi innoxii,; fin.: sacras innoxia laurus vescar,; .—
With prep. a and abl.: gens a saevo serpentum innoxia morsu,: faba a curculionibus innoxia,.—Adv.: in-noxĭē.
Harmlessly, without harm: emollire alvum,.—
Blamelessly, innocently, .

la:verb:innecto.gloss: to bind, tie, join, connect or fasten to, together or about
senses: to bind, tie, join, connect or fasten to, together or about
la:verb:innecto.html:
in-necto, nexŭi, nexum, 3 (innectier for innecti, ), v. a.,
to tie, join, bind, attach, connect, or fasten to, together, or about.
Lit.: paribus palmas amborum innexuit armis,: colla auro,: tempora sertis,to deck, garland,: fauces laqueo,to encircle,: colla lacertis,: bracchia collo,: ambos innectens manibus,: mancipia compedibus,: innecti cervicibus, to fasten upon, cling to, or embrace the neck, ; cf.: tunc placuit caesis innectere vincula silvis,; v. Orelli ad .— With acc.: nodos et vincula rupit, Queis innexa pedem malo pendebat ab alto,: vipereum crinem vittis innexa cruentis,.—
Trop.
In gen., to connect one thing with another, adduce or devise successively, weave, frame, contrive: causas innecte morandi,: moras,: fraudem clienti,.—
In partic.
To entangle, implicate: innexus conscientiae alicujus,.—
To join, connect: Hyrcanis per affinitatem innexus erat,: motus animi innexi implicatique vigoribus quibusdam mentium,: mentem, i. e. veneficio illigare,.

la:verb:inno.html:
in-no, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n.,
to swim or float in or upon.
Lit.
Partim submersae, partim fluitantes et innantes beluae, : innare contextis ratibus,: innabant pariter fluctusque secabant,: innare aquae,: fluviis, Col. poët. 10, 388. — Of vessels, a fleet, etc.: quo levior classis vadoso mari innaret,: pelago,.—With acc.: rapaces fluvios,: fluvium vinclis innaret Cloelia ruptis,. — With abl.: aquā,.—
To flow upon, to wash: innantem Maricae littoribus Lirim,.—
Transf., to sail upon, navigate: Stygios lacus,.

la:adj:innumerus.html:
in-nŭmĕrus, a, um, adj.,
countless, innumerable, numberless.
In gen. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose; false reading instead of meri,; v. Orell. and Klotz): numerus,: scaena est deserta, dein Risus, Ludu' jocusque, et numeri innumeri simul omnes collacrumarunt, verses without number, Plaut. or Varr. ap. : pecunia,: innumeras adversariorum copias superare,; : turba,: post proelii innumeras caedes,: gentes populique,; : pyrae,; miles,; ; : multitudo populorum,.—
In partic., without metre, prosaic: innumeros numeros doctis accentibus effer,.

la:verb:innuo.gloss: to give a nod, sign; to hint with a gesture
senses: to give a nod, sign; to hint with a gesture
la:verb:innuo.html:
in-nŭo, ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. n.,
to give a nod, to nod to; to give a sign, to intimate, hint.
With dat.: ubi ego innuero vobis,: abiens innuit mihi,: stabat innuebat digito similis vocanti,.—
Absol.: ne mora sit, si innuerim, quin pugnus in mala haereat,: ubi innuerint,: coram licet innuat atque Rescribat,: aqua innuetur his signis esse tenus,ext.—
To mean, intimate, signify, = significo, Don. ad .

la:adj:innocuus.html:
in-nŏcŭus, a, um, adj.,
harmless, innocuous (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.
Act.: luporum genus innocuum homini,: imber leguminibus,: iter,: litus,safe,.—
Pass., unharmed, uninjured: sedere carinae omnes innocuae,: fida per innocuas errent incendia turres,. —
Transf., inoffensive, innocent: viximus innocuae,: agere causas innocuas,to defend the innocent,: innocuum perforat ense latus,. — Hence, adv.: innŏcŭē.
Harmlessly: sagittas tanta arte direxit, ut omnes per intervalla digitorum innocue evaderent,. —
Innocently: vivere,.

la:verb:innotesco.html:
in-nōtesco, tui, 3,
v. inch. n.
To become known or noted.
With abl.: fraude,: nostris innotuit illa libellis,: petulanti pictura,: sceleribus,ext.—
Absol.: quod ubi innotuit,: carmina quae vulgo innotuerunt,; . —
Transf., of daylight, to become clear: innotescente jam luce,—
(I. q. cognosco.) To come to know, to learn by experience, .

la:adj:innocens.html:
in-nŏcens, entis, adj. (
gen. plur. innocentūm, ; but innocentium,), that does no harm.
Lit., harmless, inoffensive, innoxious (syn. insons): epistula,: ruina,: innocentis pocula Lesbii,: innocentior cibus,.—
Transf., that harms no one, blameless, guiltless, innocent.
In gen.: servus, Plant. Capt. 3, 5, 7:

innocens is dicitur, non qui leviter nocet, sed qui nihil nocet, : innocens si accusatus sit, absolvi potest,: vir integer, innocens, religiosus,: parricidii,: factorum innocens sum,: innocentissimo patre privatus est,: contentiones,carried on without bitterness,: vita innocentissimus,.—As subst.: innŏcens, entis, m., the guiltless man: cum innocente abstinentiā certabat (Cato),; . —

In partic., disinterested, upright: praetores,: vir innocens et industrius,; .—Hence, adv.: innŏcenter, harmlessly, blamelessly, innocently: vivere,: opes innocenter paratae,.— Comp.: omnia, quae caeduntur, innocentius decrescente luna, quam crescente fiunt,more safely, better,: agere,. — Sup.: vita innocentissime acta, Auct. Decl. ap. .

la:noun:innocentia.html:
in-nŏcentĭa, ae, f.,
harmlessness.
Lit.: ferorum animalium,: fumi graveolentis,—
Transf.
In gen., blamelessness, innocence: est innocentia affectio talis animi, quae noceat nemini,; : rigidae innocentiae Cato erat,: sola innocentia vivere,i. e. with no other support,: mutuā innocentiā tutum esse,where no one seeks to injure another,.—
In partic., uprightness, integrity, disinterestedness: quantā innocentiā debent esse imperatores,: suam innocentiam (opp. avaritiam) perpetuā vitā esse perspectam,.—
Collect. concr., innocent persons: innocentiam liberare,.

la:verb:innovo.html:
in-nŏvo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to renew, alter.
Lit.: plurima innovare instituit,—So in part. pass.: innŏ-vātus, a, um, renewed, ; —
Transf.: se ad aliquam rem, to return to a thing: se ad suam intemperantiam,.—As a translation of καινιεῖ, : vox mallei innovat aurem, the noise of the hammer is ever in his ears.

la:verb:innovo#2.html:
in-nŏvo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to renew, alter.

la:verb:innitor.html:
in-nītor, nixus or nīsus, 3, v. dep.,
to lean or rest upon, to support one's self by any thing.
Lit.
In gen.: vineis breves ad innitendum cannas circumdare,.
With dat. and abl.: innititur hastae,: fractae hastae,: scutis innixi,: templa vastis innixa columnis,: arbores radicibus innixae,: hasta innixus,: moderamine navis,.—
With in and acc.: in Pansam fratrem innixus,.—
In partic., to lean upon in order to press down, to press or bear upon: elephantus lixam genu innixus,.—
Trop.
In gen.: praecipuus, cui secreta imperatorum inniterentur,: salutem suam incolumitati Pisonis,: omnia curae tutelaeque unius innixa,: tuis promissis freti et innixi,.—
In partic., to end, terminate: syllabae nostrae in b litteram et d innituntur, .—
Innixum sidus, i. q. En gonasi, .

la:verb:innutrio.html:
in-nūtrĭo, īvi, ītum, 4, v. a.,
to nourish or bring up in any thing (post-Aug.): ne castris innutriretur et armis,.— Part. perf.: indigenae atque ipsius provinciae finibus innutriti, Cod. Th. 7, 13, 6, § 1: mari innutritus,: amplis opibus,: bellicis laudibus,: caelestium praeceptorum disciplinis,: liberalibus disciplinis,: certis ingeniis innutriri oportet,.

la:verb:innascor.gloss: to be born in, grow up in
senses: to be born in, grow up in
to arise in, originate in, be produced in
la:verb:innascor.html:
in-nascor, nātus sum, 3, v. dep.,
to be born in, to grow or spring up in a place.
Lit.: neglectis urenda filix innascitur agris,: Fauni velut innati triviis,: innata rupibus altis robora,: eodem innati solo, quod incolunt,: innata in cornibus cervi hedera,: calvitium uni tantum animalium homini, praeterquam innatum,excepting those that have it naturally,.—
Trop. (class.), to arise in, originate in, be produced in: in hac elatione animi nimia cupiditas principatus innascitur,.—Hence, P. a.: innātus, a, um, inborn, innate, inherent, natural.
With dat.: non mihi avaritia umquam innatast; satis habeo divitiarum,: innatam esse homini probitatem,: sunt ingeniis nostris semina innata virtutum,: est quaedam alacritas naturaliter innata omnibus,: affectata aliis castitas, tibi ingenita et innata,.—
With in and abl.: tantus est igitur innatus in nobis cognitionis amor,: in animis eorum insitum atque innatum esse videtur,.—
Absol.: nos habere insitam quandam, vel potius innatam cupiditatem scientiae,: innata atque insita anteponantur assumptis atque adventiciis,: affectatio innata videtur esse, non arcessita,.

la:verb:innatus.html:
in-nātus, a, um, adj.
2. in-nascor
,
not born, unborn (eccl. Lat.): innatus Deus annon et innata materia?; .

la:verb:innato.gloss: to swim or float in or upon
senses: to swim or float in or upon
la:verb:innato.html:
in-năto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to swim or float in or upon (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.
Homines flumini innatant, : aquis pluma innatans,: lactuca innatat acri Post vinum stomacho ( = supernatat, non subsidet),; cf.: dulce (vinum) stomacho innatat, austerum facilius concoquitur,.—
With acc.: undam innatat alnus,swims the stream,.—
To swim or float into: cum pisciculi parvi in concham hiantem innataverunt,. —
To flow over, overflow: Nilus fecundus innatat terrae,; so, innatat campis (Tiberis),: innatat unda freto dulcis,the fresh water flows into the sea,.—
To swim or float among, to be intermingled with: inter hos latent arteriae ... his innatant venae,.—
Trop.
Innatans illa verborum facilitas, floating on the surface, superficial, ; .—
Of the hair, to float or flow: tenui vagus innatat undā Crinis,.

2. in-nomino
,
that cannot be named, nameless (post-class.): indictus, innominabilis,; (dub.).
